fixes.explanation: That's the plot twist, friend. You hear that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown, and you brace for a cold shoulder, and then the Galileans welcome Him. John adds that they had seen all the great things He had done in Jerusalem at the feast, for they had gone there as well. Hometown crowds can surprise you.
Feeding a crowd with bread isn't the moment John points back to here. John 4:46 says Cana is the place where He had turned the water into wine. Nice thinking, though, friend.

That's a real story, but it's a different one (John 9:1-7). John 4:46 ties Cana to something else: it's where Jesus had turned the water into wine. Good Bible instincts, friend, but that's not the one John points to here.
Begs, friend. That's the word John uses. John 4:47 says the official went and begged Jesus to come down and heal his son.
Orders sounds like something a royal official might do, doesn't it? But John 4:47 says he went and begged. He was a royal official, and he begged.
True, friend. John 4:47 says the official's son was about to die. It's the same verse where the official goes and begs Jesus to come down and heal him.
The seventh hour matched. The father realized it was the very hour in which Jesus had told him, "Your son will live." (John 4:53) Same hour, no gap. And John says he and all his household believed.
Not yet, friend. John 4:54 says this was now the second sign Jesus performed after coming from Judea into Galilee. Second is the number John gives.
